claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis was bishop of Salamis (also called Constantia), the metropolis of Cyprus, from approximately 367 until his death in 403.
Epiphanius was born near Eleutheropolis in Palestine, probably between 310 and 320, and died in 403 at sea while returning from Constantinople to Cyprus.
The Testament to the Citizens (Testamentum ad cives, Greek: Διαθήκη πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας) is listed among the works of Epiphanius.

The authenticity of the Testamentum ad cives is disputed; a study using the Thesaurus Linguae Graecae concluded that the text does not seem to be a product of Epiphanius's pen and tentatively suggested it may be a forgery of the early Iconoclasm period based on the testimony of John of Damascus.
The Testamentum ad cives contains instructions not to set up images in churches or in cemeteries.

There has been controversy over how many quotations attributed to Epiphanius by the Byzantine Iconoclasts were actually by him, though he was clearly strongly against some contemporary uses of images in the church.
Epiphanius was known as a strong defender of orthodoxy and gained a reputation for his struggle against beliefs he considered heretical, particularly the teachings of Origen.
